summary.short: Selected sections of the FY2024 US National Defense Authorization Act: directs Defense, State and intelligence agencies to run AI pilots, studies, reports, bug-bounty and prize competitions and create AI governance bodies; also sets AUKUS export exemptions and submarine transfers.
summary.long: Selected sections of the FY2024 National Defense Authorization Act, mostly on defense and intelligence use of AI. Defense: the Chief Digital and AI Officer must run a pilot on AI-driven aerial refueling logistics (Sec. 346) and the Secretary of the Navy a shipyard AI strategy (Sec. 350); DoD must set up a bug bounty program for foundational AI models (Sec. 1542), a generative AI detection and watermarking prize competition (Sec. 1543), and AI plans, guidance and a responsible-AI compliance process (Sec. 1544); Sec. 1545 requires a vulnerability study; Sec. 1521 creates a CDAO Governing Council and CDAO data control; Sec. 1524 requires a content provenance course and pilot for DoD media. Intelligence: DNI AI policies (Sec. 7513) and AI-oriented microelectronics research (Sec. 7507). Other: a State Department Chief AI Officer (Sec. 6303) and an Office of Strategic Capital making loans for critical technologies (Sec. 903). AUKUS provisions add oversight offices, an AECA section 38(l) licensing exemption for certified partners that ends after 15 years, expedited export licence review and submarine transfers. Most duties start on enactment with deadlines from 30 days to one year; several pilots and prize authorities terminate between 2025 and 2028.
